scan.summary: This is Cascade Specialty Chemicals' emergency action plan for its Portland facility, revised February 2021. It covers what employees must do in response to fire, chemical release, medical emergency, earthquake, or other emergencies, addressing alarm systems, evacuation procedures, accountability, rescue and medical response, and training. The plan applies to all 42 employees, contractors, and visitors at the facility.
scan.freshness_note: This plan was last revised in February 2021, nearly six years ago as of September 2026. Oregon Administrative Rules 437-002-0131 requires the plan to be reviewed and updated to remain current. A plan this old should be reviewed and updated now.

gaps.title: Plan not current — last revised February 2021
gaps.description: The plan is more than five years old and has not been updated since February 2021. Oregon Administrative Rules 437-002-0131 requires emergency action plans to be reviewed and updated to remain current. Section 6 states the facilities lead reviews the plan every January, but no evidence of reviews or updates after February 2021 has been provided.
gaps.fix: Conduct a formal review and update of the plan in 2026. Document the review date and any changes made. Update the revision date on the cover. Review should address whether the employee count, floor warden and responder assignments, facility layout, alarm system details, and all procedures remain accurate.

gaps.title: No documented evidence of floor warden and first-aid responder training
gaps.description: Section 6 states that floor wardens and first-aid responders are trained annually, but no training records, dates, agendas, or evidence of this training are provided. Oregon Administrative Rules 437-002-0131(6) requires that employees with special responsibilities under the emergency action plan be trained, and that training must be documented.
gaps.fix: Maintain records of all annual training for floor wardens and first-aid responders. Each record should show the date, trainer, attendees, topics covered, and method of instruction. Keep these records for at least three years.
gaps.quote: Floor wardens and first-aid responders are trained annually.

gaps.title: No documented evidence of evacuation drill records
gaps.description: Section 4 states that evacuation drills are held twice a year (spring and autumn), but no drill records, attendance logs, timing data, or findings from those drills are provided. Oregon Administrative Rules 437-002-0131(5) requires that emergency drills be conducted and documented.
gaps.fix: Maintain a written record of each evacuation drill. Each record should include the date, time, number of participants, duration of evacuation, problems or near-misses observed, and corrective actions taken. File these records with the emergency action plan.
gaps.quote: Evacuation drills are held twice a year, in spring and autumn.

gaps.title: Evacuation map and floor warden roster not provided with this document
gaps.description: The plan references Appendix A (evacuation maps for warehouse, laboratory, and offices) and Appendix B (floor warden and first-aid responder roster), but these appendices are not included in the document provided. Oregon Administrative Rules 437-002-0131(3) and (4) require that the emergency action plan include a floor plan showing exits and assembly points and identify the person(s) responsible for implementing the plan.
gaps.fix: Provide copies of Appendix A (evacuation maps) and Appendix B (floor warden and first-aid responder roster) as part of the complete emergency action plan. The maps should clearly mark exits, assembly points, and evacuation routes for each area. The roster should list names and contact information for each floor warden and first-aid responder, with their assigned areas and shifts.
gaps.quote: Appendix A: Evacuation maps (warehouse, laboratory, offices) / Appendix B: Floor warden and first-aid responder roster (posted beside each evacuation map)

gaps.title: No specification of incident coordinator identity or current contact information
gaps.description: Sections 3, 4, and 5 reference an 'incident coordinator' who is responsible for receiving unaccounted-for reports, communicating with the fire department, and authorizing re-entry. However, the plan does not identify who the incident coordinator is, provide their name, title, or contact information, or specify a backup if the primary coordinator is not on-site. Oregon Administrative Rules 437-002-0131(3) requires identification of the person(s) responsible for implementing the plan.
gaps.fix: Add a section identifying the incident coordinator by name and title, and provide a current phone number or other contact method. Also specify a backup incident coordinator and their contact information. Update this information whenever responsibilities change. Make sure the incident coordinator is identifiable to all employees and present or reachable during all shifts.
gaps.locator: Sections 3 and 4 (incident coordinator mentioned but not identified)
gaps.quote: the incident coordinator at the assembly point, who passes the information to the fire department on arrival

gaps.title: No procedure for communication with off-site drivers
gaps.description: Section 1 states that the plan applies to 'warehouse, drivers, laboratory and office staff,' and later text refers to drivers as part of the workforce. However, the plan does not address how drivers who are away from the facility (on the road making deliveries or pickups) are notified of emergencies, how they account for themselves, or what they should do in response to a facility emergency. Oregon Administrative Rules 437-002-0131 requires the emergency action plan to address all occupants and personnel.
gaps.fix: Add a section on procedures for off-site drivers. Specify: how the incident coordinator or another designated person will contact drivers if there is an emergency; what drivers should do if contacted (report to a safe location, return to the facility, or follow other instructions); how drivers will report their location and status; and how the incident coordinator will account for all drivers. Consider whether drivers should carry a card with emergency procedures and the incident coordinator's phone number.
gaps.locator: Section 1 (scope mentions drivers), Sections 3-4 (evacuation procedures do not address drivers)
gaps.quote: all 42 employees at the Portland facility, including warehouse, drivers, laboratory and office staff

gaps.title: No documented evidence of monthly fire alarm testing
gaps.description: Section 2 states that the alarm 'is tested on the first Monday of each month by the facilities lead,' but no test records, dates, or results are provided. The Oregon Fire Code (based on the International Fire Code) requires monthly testing and documentation. Oregon Administrative Rules 437-002-0131 requires that the emergency action plan address alarm systems.
gaps.fix: Maintain a monthly fire alarm test log. After each test, document: the date, time, person who performed the test, which components were tested (horn, strobe, pull stations), whether all components functioned correctly, any problems found, and corrective actions taken. Keep these records on file.
gaps.citation: Oregon Fire Code (IFC Section 907.5); Oregon Administrative Rules 437-002-0131
gaps.quote: The alarm is tested on the first Monday of each month by the facilities lead.

gaps.title: No procedure for accounting for contractors and visitors
gaps.description: Section 1 states the plan applies to 'contractors and visitors while on site,' and Section 4 mentions that the receptionist brings out the 'visitor log' and floor wardens conduct a headcount. However, the plan does not specify how contractors and visitors are identified, how the visitor log is maintained, when it is updated, where the log is kept when not in use, or how the incident coordinator determines if a visitor is unaccounted for. Oregon Administrative Rules 437-002-0131 requires that all occupants be accounted for.
gaps.fix: Add a procedure for contractors and visitors. Specify: that all contractors and visitors must sign in with the receptionist and provide their name, company, host employee, and time of arrival; that the sign-in log is updated when they leave; where the log is kept and how it is retrieved during an evacuation; and that floor wardens will cross-reference the current occupants in the building against the sign-in log to identify who should be at the assembly point.
gaps.quote: applies to all 42 employees at the Portland facility, including warehouse, drivers, laboratory and office staff, and to contractors and visitors while on site

scan.confidence_notes: High confidence in identifying this as an emergency action plan that is substantially outdated (last revised February 2021, over five years ago). High confidence in the gaps related to missing documentation (training records, drill records, alarm test logs, appendices) because these are explicitly required by Oregon Administrative Rules 437-002-0131 and are not provided with this document. High confidence that the plan is missing specifics on incident coordinator identity, off-site driver procedures, and contractor/visitor accounting procedures, because the plan references these elements but does not detail them. The basis for each gap is either read directly from the document or logically inferred from what the document explicitly mentions but does not fully address. The citation to Oregon Administrative Rules 437-002-0131 is standard for workplace emergency action plans in Oregon and should be verified against the current rule version, which I have not independently confirmed in this response.

CASCADE SPECIALTY CHEMICALS, LLC
EMERGENCY ACTION PLAN
Portland Facility, 4410 NW Front Avenue, Portland, Oregon 97210
Revised February 2021
1. Purpose and scope
This Emergency Action Plan describes what employees of Cascade Specialty Chemicals do when there is
a fire, chemical release, medical emergency, earthquake or other emergency at the Portland facility. It
applies to all 42 employees at the Portland facility, including warehouse, drivers, laboratory and office
staff, and to contractors and visitors while on site. The plan is kept in the front office and in the warehouse
break room, and a copy is available to any employee on request.
2. Alarm system
The building has a monitored fire alarm system with audible horns and strobe lights in the warehouse,
laboratory, loading dock and offices. The alarm is monitored 24 hours a day by Cascade Fire & Safety
under a service contract. Manual pull stations are located at each exit door. The alarm is tested on the first
Monday of each month by the facilities lead. A continuous horn means evacuate. Three short horns
repeated means shelter in place because of an outdoor hazard.
3. Evacuation procedures
When the continuous alarm sounds, all employees stop work, secure nothing that requires more than a
few seconds, and leave by the nearest marked exit. Exit routes are posted on the evacuation maps at each
exit door and in Appendix A. Warehouse staff leave by the east dock doors or the north pedestrian door.
Laboratory staff leave by the laboratory's own exterior door on the south wall. Office staff leave by the
main entrance or the west stairwell. Do not use the freight lift. Do not return for belongings.
The assembly point is the far north end of the visitor parking lot, beside the flagpole, at least 150 feet
from the building. Employees assigned as floor wardens (one per area, listed on the warden roster posted
beside each evacuation map) sweep their area, close doors behind them, and report to the assembly point.
For a chemical release outdoors or a hazard that makes leaving the building unsafe, the shelter-in-place
signal sounds. Employees move to the interior conference room or the laboratory corridor, close doors,
and the facilities lead shuts down the building ventilation from the mechanical room panel.
4. Accounting for employees after evacuation
At the assembly point each floor warden takes a headcount of the people from their area against the daily
sign-in sheet and the visitor log, which the receptionist brings out. Any person unaccounted for is reported
at once to the incident coordinator at the assembly point, who passes the information to the fire
department on arrival. No one re-enters the building until the fire department or the incident coordinator
gives the all-clear. Evacuation drills are held twice a year, in spring and autumn.
5. Rescue and medical duties
Employees do not attempt rescue inside the building. First aid is given at the assembly point by the
trained first-aid responders (two per shift, named on the warden roster), who bring the first-aid kit and the
AED from the front office. An employee exposed to a chemical is taken to the emergency shower and
eyewash at the loading dock if it can be reached safely, or to the assembly point, and the SDS for the
product is brought to the responders. Emergency medical services are called for any injury beyond minor
first aid.
6. Training and review
Every new employee is walked through this plan, the exit routes for their work area and the assembly
point on their first day. Floor wardens and first-aid responders are trained annually. The plan is reviewed
with all employees whenever it is changed and whenever an employee's responsibilities under it change.
The facilities lead reviews the plan every January and updates the evacuation maps whenever the building
layout changes.
Appendix A: Evacuation maps (warehouse, laboratory, offices)
Appendix B: Floor warden and first-aid responder roster (posted beside each evacuation map)
